d: Magnificent atrium in the ducal palace in Ferrara. Among the columns you can see the doors of the apartments on the ground. The first on the right is of the Duchess Eleonora. The second is of the Countess Scandiano. On the left the first is of the Tasso, the second is of Geraldini. At the bottom is that of the Duke, before which they walk Swiss guards. Some Knights advance from the door of the Duke's apartment talking softly among them; then Don Gherardo from the colonnade at the bottom; then Ambrose from the rooms of the Tasso.
Geraldini comes out thinking: then he takes a look at the apartments of Torquato.

Apartment of Tasso. A side door is the municipality. One at the bottom leads to the inner rooms. Table with delivery to write, volumes, and scattered papers, and a petiole box ironed closed. Chairs. Torquato slowly progressed as absorbed in thoughts of love.
Ambrose from the municipality precedes Roberto, who prevents him from announcing him by spotting Torquato in a moment of poetic inspiration. Geraldini, Torquato.
Ambrose on the middle door.
Geraldini solo; indi don Gherardo from the municipality.
Don Gherardo solo; then Ambrose.

Noble room in the apartment of woman Eleonora sister of the Duke, in whose walls are painted some facts expressed by Torquato in Goffredo. Three doors in the bottom adorned with rich curtains. Table with rich carpet, books, and a vase of flowers. Chairs around. Eleonora woman advances with a volume of the poem manuscript of Torquato in her hands.
The Countess Eleonora of Scandiano from one of the side doors, is said.
Eleonora alone, then the Tasso who stops at the middle door.
A page of the Duke presented himself on the middle door with a sealed envelope. The Duchess now speaks to the page, and now stealthy to Tasso.
Geraldini from the middle, then the Duchess, and Don Gherardo.
Paggi and Cortigiani from the middle door, before the Duke.

Land Gallery in Belriguardo with a view of part of the ducal gardens. Shortly in the evening. The Cortigiani, from various parts enter the scene, and with caution they gather on the front talking to each other.
The voice of the Countess of Scandiano is heard, who enters the scene wanting to escape Don Gherardo. The courtiers in attention withdraw, and when they advance to hear.
The Duke is said, and the courtiers are hidden.
The Duchess, and Ambrose.
Eleonora alone, then Geraldini.
The Duke alone, concentrated in his thoughts; then Geraldini.

In the end an Apollo mentioned in marble above a great source from which flow clear, and copious waters. The moon thins somewhat the shadow of the night. Torquato slowly crosses. Don Gherardo from afar follows him guarding; then the Duchess.
On the one hand the Duke appears in the trees, next to which is Geraldini, and on the other hand the Scandiano led by Don Gherardo.

Room destined in prison in Torquato. In the bottom a grate of iron bars, and a door, which puts inside the room. A shelf of books in disorder. Laterally a door that introduces to the adjoining room of Torquato. A crude table with bundles of cards, volumes, and delivery to write. A scranna. From the top hangs a lamp that weakly illuminates the darkness of the old walls. Torquato comes out of the adjoining room concentrated in melancholy meditation; in the choir of Knights of the court of the Duke Alfonso II in the distance, and then on stage.
